newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan forces converge on key northern town.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan forces converge on key northern town.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops driving into Tamil Tiger guerrilla territory in the north resumed their advance on Friday, closing in on a key junction town from the east and south, security officials said.

Troops backed by tanks, artillery and air support were moving towards the heavily fortified town of Puliyankulam, about 245 km (153 miles) north of the capital Colombo, in the mostly jungle-covered Wanni region, they said.
"Troops resumed their advance further northwards from the earlier held positions at first light today," a Defence Ministry statement said on Friday.
"Satisfactory progress has been made so far and the terrorists are expected to resist the advancing troops," it said, adding the rebels had fired mortars at the soldiers.

Residents in Vavuniya, the gateway to the Wanni some 25 km (16 miles) to the south of Puliyankulam, reported hearing aircraft heading for the battlefield and the sound of artillery shells exploding in the distance.
Casualties were pouring into the town with ambulances and trucks carrying wounded racing through the streets, they said.

The troops resumed their advance from positions near Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya, and Nedunkeni, 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya. They captured the two towns in an offensive codenamed Operation Jaya Sikuru, or Sure of Victory, that was launched from Vavuniya on May 13.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte told a news conference the aim of the offensive was to open a land supply route to Jaffna, 100 km (60 miles) further north, that would help rehabilitation work there.
The north-south highway has been closed for more than 10 years due to fighting between the rebels and government forces.
Ratwatte said troops had moved eight km (five miles) north of Omanthai, which army officials said was near Pandrikeithakulam village.
Military officials said Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas had vacated at least two bases along the route government troops were taking.

The LTTE, fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, accused the military in an overnight statement of systematically demolishing Tamil towns in the north.
Buildings in Nedunkeni, which the army captured after fierce fighting last month, had been blown up, it said.
"A concerted dismembering of Tamil society (town by town) is taking place, where Tamils' lifeline and self-sufficiency is progressively weakened by the Sinhala government," The LTTE statement said.

The rebels earlier said the military was firing artillery at heavily populated towns 32 km (20) miles from its forward defences, forcing civilians to abandon their homes and seek refuge in the jungle.
The military has denied their shells were aimed at civilians, saying they fired only at identified rebel targets.
The rebels also said Tamil property and food were looted by the armed forces at Nedunkeni, but the Defence Ministry spokesman denied the charge.
Independent confirmation of the events was not possible as international media have not been allowed in the war zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the war began in 1983. The rebels say the toll is higher.
